If you say: why was it not said "or you are silent" and why was the nominal sentence placed in the position of the verbal one? I say: because whenever a matter distressed them, they called upon Allah rather than their idols, as in His words ﴿and when harm touches people﴾. So their constant state was to be silent about calling on them. Hence it was said: whether you call on them or not, the state does not differ between your act of calling on them and your habitual silence about calling on them.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 7, verses 191–193:

The idols were treated as if they were beings of intellect (ulu al-'ilm) in His words "and they are created (wa-hum yukhlaqun)", based on the belief of the idolaters about them and their naming them gods (alihah). The meaning is: Do they associate with Him what cannot create anything as Allah creates, while they themselves are created? Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is their Creator. Or: it cannot create anything, because it is inanimate, while they are created, because their worshippers fashion them. So they are weaker than their worshippers. ﴿And they cannot give them help﴾, that is, to their worshippers, ﴿nor can they help themselves﴾, so that they could ward off from themselves the calamities that befall them. Rather, their worshippers are the ones who ward off harm from them and defend them. ﴿And if you call them to guidance﴾, that is, if you call these idols to guidance (hudan), namely to what is right guidance and rectitude, and to guide you. The meaning: if you seek from them, as you seek from Allah, good and guidance, they will not follow you to what you desire and seek, nor will they answer you as Allah answers you. This is indicated by His words: ﴿So let them answer you, if you are truthful. It is the same for you whether you call them or remain silent about calling on them﴾, meaning there is no success with them. If you say: why was it not said "or you are silent" and why was the nominal sentence placed in the position of the verbal one? I say: because whenever a matter distressed them, they called upon Allah rather than their idols, as in His words ﴿and when harm touches people﴾. So their constant state was to be silent about calling on them. Hence it was said: whether you call on them or not, the state does not differ between your act of calling on them and your habitual silence about calling on them.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 7, verses 194–195:

Inna alladhina tad'una min duni Allah (﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah﴾), meaning: those you worship and call gods besides Allah, ibadun amthalukum (﴿are servants like you﴾). His saying ibadun amthalukum is said mockingly towards them: the utmost of their state is that they be living and rational. If that is established, then they are servants like you, with no superiority between you. Then he refuted that they are servants like them, saying: Alahum arjulun yamshuna biha (﴿Do they have feet with which they walk?﴾). It was also said: ibadun amthalukum means "owned slaves like you."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr recited: inna alladhina tad'una min duni Allahi ibadan amthalukum, with the lightening of inna and the accusative of ibadan amthalukum, meaning: "those you invoke besides Allah are not servants like you," applying the negating inna the function of the Hijazi ma (ma al-hijaziyya).

Qul ud'u shurakaakum (﴿Say: Call upon your associates﴾) and seek their help against me, thumma kidúni jami'an (﴿then plot against me all together, you and your associates﴾), fala tunzirun (﴿and give me no respite﴾), for indeed I do not care about you. None says this except one who is confident of Allah's protection. They had threatened him with their gods, so he was commanded to address them with this, just as the people of Hud said to him: in naqulu illa i'taraka ba'du alihatina bi-su' (﴿We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil﴾). He said to them: inni bari'un mimma tushrikun min dunihi (﴿Indeed, I am free from what you associate besides Him﴾), fakidúni jami'an thumma la tunzirun (﴿so plot against me all together, then give me no respite﴾).

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 7, verses 196–197:

"Indeed, my guardian is Allah," that is, my helper against you. "He who revealed the Book," that is, the one who revealed to me His Book and honoured me with His message. "And He takes charge of the righteous," and it is His custom to support the righteous among His servants and His prophets, and not to forsake them.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 7, verses 196–197:

"Indeed, my guardian is Allah," that is, my helper against you. "He who revealed the Book," that is, the one who revealed to me His Book and honoured me with His message. "And He takes charge of the righteous," and it is His custom to support the righteous among His servants and His prophets, and not to forsake them.

They look at you, resembling those who look at you, because they fashioned their idols in the form of one whose eyeball is turned toward a thing he is looking at, **and they do not see**: and they do not perceive the visible object.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 7, verse 199:

Al-ʿafw (pardon, what is easy and readily available) is the opposite of al-juhd (exertion). That is: take what is easily available of people's actions, their characters, and what comes from them, that which is effortless, without burdening them or demanding of them exertion and what is hard for them, so that they do not flee from you. Like His saying ﷺ, "Make things easy and do not make them difficult" [[Agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh), from the hadith of Anas, more complete than this.]]. He said:

"Take what is easy from me, and your affection will endure;
and do not speak harshly in my anger when I am enraged." [[The explanation of this line of evidence has passed in the first volume, p. 362, so refer to it if you wish. Its corrector (muṣahhih) says so.]]

It was also said: take the surplus, and what is easy of their charity (ṣadaqāt). This was before the revelation of the verse on zakat; when it was revealed, he was commanded to take it from them willingly or unwillingly.

Al-ʿurf: the known good and beautiful of actions. "And turn away from the ignorant." That is, do not repay the foolish with the like of their foolishness, do not dispute with them, be forbearing toward them, and overlook what grieves you from them. It was also said:

When this verse was revealed, Jibril asked, "I do not know until I ask." [[Al-Tabari narrated it through Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna from Abu al-Muradi, who said: "When God revealed..." and so on; this is a broken chain (munqaṭiʿ). Ibn Mardawayh narrated it connected (mawṣūl) from the hadith of Jabir and from the hadith of Qays ibn Saʿd, and he added at its beginning: "When the Messenger of God ﷺ looked at Hamza, he said: 'By God, I will mutilate seventy of them for this.' Then Jibril came with this verse," and he mentioned the hadith. In the Musnad of Ahmad, from ʿUqba ibn ʿAmir, that the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "O ʿUqba, shall I not inform you of the best of the characters of the people of this world: that you join ties with the one who cut you off, give to the one who withholds from you, and pardon the one who wronged you," and al-Tibi was mistaken when he said in the hadith of the original text: Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of ʿUqba ibn ʿAmir.]] Then he returned and said: "O Muhammad, your Lord commands you to join ties with the one who cut you off, to give to the one who withholds from you, and to pardon the one who wronged you." And from Jaʿfar al-Sadiq:

God commanded His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, with the noble qualities of character, and there is no verse in the Qur'an more comprehensive of the noble qualities of character than this one.

﴿وَإِمَّا يَنْزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ نَزْغٌ﴾ and ﴿وَإِمَّا يَنْخُسَنَّكَ مِنْهُ نَخْسٌ﴾, meaning: if a prick from Satan pricks you, by his whispering that drives you to act against what you were commanded. ﴿فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ وَلَا تُطِعْهُ﴾: seek refuge in Allah and do not obey him. The words *al-nazgh* (النزغ) and *al-nasgh* (النسغ) mean to thrust or prick, as if Satan pricks people when he incites them to acts of disobedience. *Al-nazgh* is made into an agent, as in the saying *jadda jaddahu* (his striving was great). It is related that when this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How, O Lord, and anger?" So ﴿وَإِمَّا يَنْزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ نَزْغٌ﴾ was revealed. [[Al-Tabari related it from the narration of Ibn Wahb from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, "when it was revealed," and mentioned it in detail.]]

It is also permissible that the Satan's prick be understood as the onset of anger, as in the words of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him): "Indeed, I have a devil who overtakes me." [[Ishaq ibn Rahawayh related it in his Musnad, and Ibn Saʿd in al-Tabaqat, both saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, I heard al-Hasan say: "Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) addressed the people one day and said: 'As for me, by Allah, I am not the best of you, and I was unwilling for this position of mine. I wished that among you there were someone who would suffice me, so that I could act among you by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for which I would be fit to rise. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was supported by revelation, and an angel was with him. Indeed, I have a devil who overtakes me. So when I become angry, avoid me.'" The hadith. ʿAbd al-Razzaq related it from Maʿmar from a man from al-Hasan, similar to it. We also have it in the Juz' of al-Ansari through the chain of Abu Hilal from al-Hasan, who said: "When Abu Bakr was made caliph, he began with a speech by Allah, which no one other than him had ever spoken," and he mentioned something similar.]]

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 7, verses 201–202:

﴿A visitation from Satan﴾: the word *talif* (ṭayf) is a verbal noun (maṣdar) from their saying: "The phantom (khayāl) visited him" (ṭāf bihi al-khayāl yaṭīfu ṭayfan). He said:

"How did the phantom come to you in the night, visiting? And its visiting you is remembrance and passion..."

It is said of Ka'b ibn Zuhayr. *Anā* here is an interrogative of wonder, meaning "how" or "from where." *Alamma*: he came down to visit. *Al-khayāl*: what the sleeper sees. *Ṭāfa bihi al-khayāl yaṭīfu ṭayfan wa maṭāfan*: it approached him. *Ṭāfa ḥawlahu yaṭūfu ṭawāfan wa ṭūfānan*: it hovered around him and circled him, and it is used as a metaphor for touching. His saying *yaṭīfu* is a circumstantial clause (jumla ḥāliyya), either emphatic or establishing. *Maṭāfuhu*: that is, its phantom is the cause of remembrance and the arrival of love at the innermost heart, so the effect is put in the place of the cause. He referred to himself first with the third-person pronoun and then with the second person, by way of *iltifāt* (shift of person), to flee from the suspicion of repetition. It is also narrated as *bik* (with the second person).

Or it is a lightened form of *ṭayyif* (fayʿal), from *ṭāfa yaṭīfu*, like *layyin* becoming *layn*. Or from *ṭāfa yaṭūfu*, like *hayyin*. It is also read as *ṭā'if*, which likewise allows both meanings. This is an affirmation and confirmation of what preceded regarding the obligation of seeking refuge in God when Satan's prick (nazgh) occurs, and that this is the habit of the God-fearing: when even a slight prick from Satan and a touch of his whispering befall them, they remember what God has commanded and forbidden, so they see the right course and repel what he whispered to them, and their own selves do not follow him. As for the brothers of the devils, who are not God-fearing, the devils extend them in error (*yamudduhum fi al-ghayy*), that is, they become a supply for them in it and reinforce them. It is also read as *yumiddūnahum* from *al-imdād*, and *yumādddūnahum*, meaning they assist them. *Thumma lā yuqṣirūn*: then they do not refrain from their misguidance, until they persist and do not return.

His saying *wa-ikhwānuhum yamuddūnahum* is like the saying of the poet:

"A people who, when the horses wheel in their charges, are horsemen who neither sway nor are weak..."

*Al-khayl* means the mares. *Al-kāthiba* is the withers of a horse; for a camel it is the hump (*al-gharib*), and for a man the shoulder-blades (*al-kāhil*). The donkey has *al-sīsiyā*.

*Al-mayl* is the plural of *amyal*, one who does not stay firm on his horse's back. *Al-qadam* is the plural of *aqdam*, the base and weak one; or the plural of *qadam* with a sukūn, with the same meaning. The pronoun in *jālū* refers to the people, so the predicate is applied to other than what it belongs to. That is, when the horses wheel, they are in their saddles. The pronoun is not made explicit in this way because its required place is in the adjective and not the verb, or to avoid ambiguity, since the *wāw* is the pronoun of rational beings. If it is objected that *idhā* is only followed by a verbal clause, so *al-khayl* is the subject of a deleted verb, the answer is: it is not granted that it is only followed by a verbal clause, and that applies to the conditional *idhā*, not the temporal *idhā* as here. It is said, though far-fetched, that *al-khayl* may mean the horsemen, and the pronoun in *kawāthibihā* refers to the mares indicated by the mention of *al-khayl*: that is, a people who, when the horsemen wheel over the charges of the mares, are horsemen who remain firm upon them, not leaning from their backs, nor weak as though their hands were chained.

This shows that the predicate applies to what it belongs to. It is permissible that *al-ikhwān* be understood as the devils, with the pronoun attached to it referring to the ignorant, so that the predicate applies to what it belongs to; but the first is more apt, because *ikhwānuhum* stands in contrast to *alladhīna ittaqaw*. If you ask: why is the pronoun in *ikhwānuhum* plural when *al-shayṭān* is singular? I say: it is meant as a collective noun, as in His saying: *awliyāʾuhumu al-ṭāghūt* (their protectors are the transgressor).

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 7, verse 203:

"Ijtabā al-shay'" (اجتبى الشيء), in the sense of "jabāhu li-nafsihi" (he took it for himself), means: he gathered it, as when you say "ijtama'ahu" (he gathered it together). Or it means "jabā ilayhi fa-ijtabāhu" (he collected it toward himself and then took it), that is, he took it, as when you say "jallaytu ilayhi al-'arūs fa-ijtallāhā" (I displayed the bride to him and he took her).

The meaning of "lawlā ijtabaytahā" (لَوْلا اجْتَبَيْتَها) is: "Why did you not gather it?", as a fabrication (iftiʿāl) from yourself, because they used to say, "This is nothing but a fabricated lie" (مَا هَذَا إِلَّا إِفْكٌ مُفْتَرًى). Or: "Why did you not take it, sent down to you as something proposed?"

﴿Say: I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord.﴾ (قُلْ إِنَّمَا أَتَّبِعُ مَا يُوحَى إِلَيَّ مِنْ رَبِّي) — meaning, I am not one who fabricates the verses, or: I am not one who proposes them.

﴿This Qur'an is insights (baṣāʾir) from your Lord﴾ (هَذَا بَصَائِرُ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) — that is, clear proofs (ḥujaj bayyina) by which believers come to see after blindness. Or it is in the position of the insights of the hearts (baṣāʾir al-qulūb).

﴿When the Qur'an is recited, listen to it attentively and be silent﴾

Its apparent meaning is that listening and remaining silent are obligatory whenever the Qur'an is recited, both in prayer and outside prayer. It was said: the verse was revealed because people used to talk during the prayer. Then it became a sunnah outside prayer that the people be silent when they are in a gathering where the Qur'an is recited. It was also said that its meaning is: ﴿When the Messenger recites the Qur'an to you as it is being revealed, listen to it.﴾ It was further said that the meaning of "listen to it" is: act upon what is in it, and do not transgress it.

**Remember your Lord within yourself**, meaning: this is general, covering all forms of remembrance: recitation of the Qur'an, supplication, glorifying God (tasbih), declaring His oneness (tahlil), and other things. **Humbly and in fear**: humbly and fearfully. **And without speaking aloud**: speaking in a voice below the loud, because concealment is more conducive to sincerity (ikhlas, "sincerity of intention") and closer to good reflection. **In the mornings and evenings**: because of the excellence of these two times. Or it means constancy. The meaning of **bil-ghuduw** ("in the mornings") is: at the times of the morning, which are the mornings. It was also read:

**wal-iy'sal**, from **aṣala** when one enters the **aṣil** (late afternoon), like **aqṣara** (he entered the qaṣr, the evening) and **a'tama** (he entered the 'atma, the time of the night prayer). [The note: "His words 'like aqṣara and a'tama': aqṣara means he entered the qaṣr, that is the evening, and a'tama means he entered the 'atma, that is the time of the night prayer. Recorded by al-Ṣiḥāḥ." (ʿ)] This is parallel to **al-ghuduw**. **And do not be among the heedless**: among those who are unmindful of the remembrance of God and distracted from it.

Indeed, those who are with your Lord are the angels, may the blessings of God be upon them. The meaning of "with" (ʿinda) is the nearness of rank and closeness to God's mercy and grace, because they devote themselves to His obedience and to seeking His pleasure. "And to Him they prostrate" means that they single Him out for worship and do not associate anyone with Him. This is an implicit rebuke to those others among the accountable beings who do not do so.

From the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat al-A'raf, God will make between him and Iblis a screen on the Day of Resurrection, and Adam will be his intercessor on the Day of Resurrection." [Its chains of transmission were mentioned in the commentary on Surat Aal 'Imran, and it will come again at the end of the book.]
